Patch C26: the folder fingerprint -- what it covers, what changes it, what makes a folder untrustworthy.

The fingerprint is the thing a trust decision is tied to, so these tests pin three properties:

* STABLE: the same listed files give the same digest, wherever the folder lives and in whatever order the files were made,
  and the digest is the documented SHA-256 construction (a reference implementation below), so a release can never silently
  change what an old stored decision means.
* SENSITIVE: a changed byte, a renamed, added or deleted listed file all change it; a file outside the listed places does not.
* SAFE: symlinks, over-large trees, odd files and odd names never raise, never hang, never follow a link out of the project,
  and make the folder "cannot be trusted automatically" instead of producing a digest.

Patch P00 (M2C Wave 1) -- validator for the M2C protocol and tool-schema contract.

protocol/v1/ is the ONE source of truth for the wire format between the device
client (m2c/) and the server (backend/codeagent/, WP S04/S05/S09). This script
is the reference reader of it:

    python protocol/validate.py                    # everything below, exit 0/1
    python protocol/validate.py --check-client-copy
    python protocol/validate.py --sync-client

Default run checks, in order:
  1. every schema under protocol/v1 is a well-formed Draft 2020-12 schema whose
     $id matches its path, every $ref resolves, every tool definition fits
     tool_definition.json, and every v0 tool has a tool_proposed branch;
  2. every golden transcript (protocol/fixtures/*.jsonl) validates line by line
     AND as a transcript (check_transcript: seq runs, call-id pairing, resume
     cursors, terminal states);
  3. every case in fixtures/invalid_examples.jsonl FAILS, and fails on the
     keyword and path it names (so a broken example cannot pass for the wrong
     reason);
  4. the client's synced copy of the schemas, if the m2c/ package exists yet,
     is byte-identical (see compare_client_copy).

--check-client-copy runs only step 4. It passes when m2c/src/m2c/protocol/v1/
does not exist yet: WP C01 creates the client package in parallel with this
patch, so on a tree without it there is nothing to compare.

--sync-client copies protocol/v1/**/*.json over the client copy (and removes
stale .json

codebase_census.py - measure everything about a repo, from the LOCAL working copy.

Usage (from the repo root):   python scripts/codebase_census.py
Output:                       graphify-out/census.json   (git-ignored)

Reads only source structure + git metadata. It never records file contents,
secret values or .env values (only variable NAMES). Standard library only;
if `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-javascript` are installed (Graphify installs
them) JS/JSX is parsed exactly, otherwise a heuristic fallback is used.

script_version 2 (additive; every v1 field keeps its meaning) adds, per symbol:
  doc1 (first docstring/JSDoc sentence, <= 200 chars), params, returns, raises, calls
  ([name, "path::qual" | null] pairs), hash (10 hex of the whitespace-normalised source),
  visibility (public | private | dunder), hooks_used / exported (JS), qual + method_names +
  hash (classes). Per file: module_doc up to 1500 chars, exports (Python). Top level:
  table_refs (SQL table -> files whose code mentions it) and git.head_full (40 hex).
Join key for a symbol is "<path>::<qual>". When a file defines the same qual twice
(property setters, conditional redefinitions) the later ones become qual~2, qual~3 ... in
source order. Parameter defaults are recorded only when they are short literals or bare
names and the parameter name is not secret-looking; otherwise they are the string "...".

backend/pyproject.toml.raw_head:
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Pinned per ci.yml's own header comment. A prior change (see git
# history / PR discussion for "B3") briefly moved this repo onto
# ruff's zero-config default rule set, which as of ruff 0.16 enables
# nearly every rule family (813 findings on this repo vs. 13 under
# this pinned selection, measured 2026-08-25 on ruff 0.16.4) -- but
# the two cleanup batches that change's own comment described (an
# auto-fix pass, then a manual-triage pass for RUF013/BLE001-style
# judgment calls) were never landed, so CI was red on every push
# regardless of what else changed. Reverted to the pinned selection to
# unblock CI now; broadening this again should ship together with the
# actual cleanup, not ahead of it.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# This module borrows the `store` fixture from test_eo_code_proposals_deploy
# (imported, not moved), so every test taking `store` as an argument looks
# like a redefinition of an unused import to F811. That is how pytest
# fixture injection works, not a real shadowing bug.
"tests/unit/test_eo_code_proposals_wireframe.py" = ["F811"]

m2c/pyproject.toml.raw_head:
# m2c/pyproject.toml -- Patch C01: packaging for the M2C client.
#
# Build backend: hatchling. Chosen over setuptools because this is a pure-
# Python src-layout package with no compiled code and no setup.py quirks:
# PEP 517/660 editable installs work out of the box (`pip install -e .`),
# the version is read from one line in src/m2c/__init__.py without importing
# it, and `uv tool install` / `pipx` build it the same way. Pinned exactly,
# like the other tools in this repo (ruff, the CI actions): bump it
# deliberately, and prefer a release at least a couple of weeks old.
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling==1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "m2c"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "M2C (Minime to Code): a local-first coding agent client for Linux and WSL2."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"            # decision D1
# Runtime dependencies: the standard library only, plus THREE exceptions.
# tests/test_cli.py fails if another is added here (or imported) without that
# test being changed on purpose.  The exception (Patch C04): ``websockets``, the
# WebSocket client of the device link (m2c/link), pinned exactly like
# daemon/requirements.txt so the two packages cannot drift; only m2c/link may
# import it.  Patch C09 adds ``prompt_toolkit`` and ``rich``, the terminal chat
# (decision D2); only m2c/tui/app.py imports them, and cli.py imports that
# module lazily, so headless mode and every other command never l
